subject: Issues with Umbrella Sampling Simulations involving lipid bilayer

messages.author: Casalini  Tommaso
messages.body:
Dear Amber users and developers,
I am performing Umbrella Sampling simulations to study the permeation of a small polymer fragment inside a POPC/CHL 2:1 lipid bilayer.
I built the lipid bilayer with the CHARMM GUI website and I have obtained an equilibrated structure, that I checked with the area per lipid and bilayer thickness as a function of simulation time.
I have subsequently put the polymer fragment in the simulation box and I have rebuilt the simulation box with the AddToBox utility, adding water and ions only along z.
I ran additional simulations to obtain an equilibrated system configuration and I started US simulations.
I use the following input file:

&cntrl
imin = 0,
irest = 1,
ntx = 7,
ntb = 2,
pres0 = 1.0,
ntp = 3,

DISANG = ref_COM.rst
DUMPAVE = Pull_dist.dat
LISTIN = POUT
LISTOUT = POUT
/
/

/

Can you provide some suggestions?
I thank you in advance for your support!
Tommaso

messages.author: Stephan Schott
messages.body:
Hi Tommaso,
Are you using sander, pmemd or pmemd.cuda? What AMBER version are you
using, and which patches have been applied? I remember there was an issue
with COM restraints, fixed in update 13 of AMBER 18. You could try
increasing the rate at which you save the trajectory frames, to take a look
at the moment when the RESTRAINT energy goes crazy.
Cheers,

I am using the pmemd.cuda module of AMBER16, without additional patches.

As mentioned in the previous mail, what puzzles me is that I used the same approach using a different membrane (pure DOPC) and everything went well.
Best,
Tommaso

Dear Stephan,
right now the restraint is aimed at keeping the polymer COM/bilayer COM distance at 0 (as shown but the input file that I copied).

The output file with the distances is correctly written, the distance is equal to about 0.
If necessary, I can share my files to check if someone can reproduce my issue.

I don't currently have the bandwidth to backport patches to older versions of amber. You can try porting update.13 backwards to amber 16 as I wrote that patch a few days after the thread listed below: https://ambermd.org/bugfixes/18.0/update.13

Charlie
